title: The story of AMUL
body: In the early 1940s, dairy farmers in Anand district of Gujarat had to cycle or walk to nearby villages to sell their milk in scorching heat. Milk spoils quickly in hot weather, so they had to sell it fast. Middlemen bought the milk in bulk at very low prices and sold it in the market, and the farmers often felt cheated. The farmers went to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who advised them to form a cooperative. AMUL was set up in 1946 under the leadership of Tribhuvandas Patel and Dr. Varghese Kurien. The members, including women, now decided together on production, pasteurisation and sale of milk. As more milk was collected, they set up a factory in Anand to make butter and milk powder. Today the products are carried by trucks, railways, air and ships to shops across India and are also exported to other countries.
